NVIDIA:893398215059.title: Agent Evaluation and Self-Improvement Engineer
NVIDIA:893398215059.description:
Autonomous agents now do real work across NVIDIA, and every piece underneath them keeps changing: models, harnesses, tools, skills, and plugins. Evaluation is how a team knows whether a change made an agent better or quietly made it worse. We're looking for a principal engineer to set evaluation strategy at every layer, from individual skills and MCP servers to whole agents and products, and to design how agents use those results to improve themselves.

  


Agents can already rewrite the skills and plugins they run on, then test whether the change helped. Making that loop trustworthy is the hard part. What does it take for an agent to get better on its own, and prove the improvement is real? We're building a system that answers that question for every agent at NVIDIA. Come build it with us!

  


What you'll be doing:

  * Build evaluation that works the same across harnesses, with automated checks on every change that catch regressions before users do.
  * Mine production traces for failures, new usage patterns, missing skills and tools, cost and latency hot spots, and successful runs. Turn them into eval cases and improvement signals.
  * Evaluate the eval datasets themselves: coverage of real usage, duplicate cases, and how closely they match production.
  * Build the self-improvement loop for evolving harnesses: agents propose changes to their own skills, plugins, and harness configuration, and sandboxed evals test each one. Only measurable gains ship, with human sign-off and limits agents can't change.
  * Create realistic enterprise environments: sandboxed replicas of issue trackers, code repositories, chat, and internal APIs, filled with synthetic or anonymized data, where agents safely run long, end-to-end tasks.
  * Measure multi-agent swarms as a team: how agents split work, whether handoffs succeed, and whether permissions hold at every hop. Record how long each task takes and how many tokens it uses.
  * Keep evals honest: calibrate model and agent judges against human labels. Catch agents that cheat, such as working backward from expected answers or reaching data and tools they shouldn't access. Available Locations: London or Lisbon About the Department Emerging Technologies & Incubation (ETI) is where new and bold products are built and released within Cloudflare. Rather than being constrained by the structures which make Cloudflare a hugely successful business, we are able to leverage them to deliver entirely new tools and products to our customers. Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization. About the Team We build the infrastructure that makes the web Payable , powering the future of machine-to-machine commerce. Here at Cloudflare, agentic commerce is a core part of our vision for the Agentic Internet . As AI agents increasingly navigate, consume, and act on the web, standard payment and authorization models built for humans are breaking down. We are building tools that help make the new internet payable by giving our users the ability to take control over how AI agents pay for resources across the Internet. Building these capabilities requires solving problems across high-throughput web infrastructure, low-latency transaction processing, digital wallets, and emerging agentic payment protocols. We bridge mainstream fiat commerce rails with decentralized protocols, enabling micro-payments at Internet scale. We’re looking for someone excited to deliver products so domain owners can control this experience, while identifying the problems Cloudflare is uniquely positioned to solve next. We are a tight-knit group that communicates and collaborates regularly. We celebrate our achievements, support each other when we make mistakes, and hold each other and our work to a high standard. You have strong product judgment and enjoy working with Product Management to decide what is worth building, what needs improvement and what should not be built at all. The role means balancing competing demands every day: build deadlines against build quality, dependence on partners against high standards, and fast incident response against careful compliance. It works closely with network engineering and server provisioning teams but does not own them. What You'll Do Team Leadership Hire, develop and manage Data Center Engineers based on-site at data centers across the US. Set clear expectations, career paths and a culture of ownership across a team spread over many sites. Build and take part in a 24x7 on-call rotation with your team. Define coverage models, handover protocols and incident SLAs that hold up as the footprint grows. Serve as the escalation point for on-site incidents. Coordinate engineers, colocation providers and vendors to restore service quickly, and lead root-cause analysis after major incidents so the same problem doesn't happen again. Site Delivery Own build timelines from site readiness through hardware delivery, rack-and-stack, cabling, validation and handoff to production. Run greenfield builds as multi-workstream programs. Coordinate third-party integrators, contractors and colocation providers to hit dates without cutting corners. Be on-site during key build phases to oversee vendor work, verify quality and make sure sites are production-ready. Production Operations Be accountable for availability targets for production hardware at your sites. Run break/fix, repairs, RMAs and spares strategy so that availability is measured, reported and improving. Manage colocation providers and vendors day to day: escalations, remote-hands quality, power and cooling issues, and performance against contractual commitments. Documentation and DCIM Make sure every site is fully documented in DCIM from day one. That covers rack elevations, power and cabling, asset location, and lifecycle status, all recorded as hardware arrives rather than filled in later. Treat infrastructure records as a source of truth that both operations and dependent teams rely on, giving them accurate, current visibility into where hardware is and what state it's in. Partner with tooling teams to bring DCIM online at new sites, and define documentation standards that hold up as the footprint grows. Decommissioning and Hardware Lifecycle Own on-site decommissioning end to end: unracking, physical collections, serial number verification, chain of custody, and handoff for secure destruction. Partner with vendor management on IT asset disposition (ITAD) vendors. Make sure destruction certificates and compliance evidence are filed and audit-ready. Security and Compliance Make sure your sites and team meet Cloudflare's physical security, access control, chain-of-custody and compliance obligations. Follow established physical access procedures, and work with security and compliance teams to develop new ones where these sites need them. Support audits with accurate, timely evidence. Treat audit readiness as a continuous standard, not something you prepare for once per audit cycle. Automation and Operational Efficiency Find manual, repetitive work in build, break/fix, decommissioning and evidence collection. Influence tooling and automation teams to remove it. Evaluate and adopt AI-assisted workflows for incident triage, root-cause analysis, documentation and compliance evidence generation. Scale the operation through tooling, not just headcount. Business Reporting Own weekly business reviews and monthly and quarterly reporting on availability, build progress, incidents and operational health to the Director and peer leaders. Partner with network, systems, hardware, supply chain and infrastructure engineering teams to make sure physical operations support what runs on top of them. Who You Are A builder who stays to operate. You've stood up sites and teams, and you take ownership of what happens after go-live. Delivering a build is where your job starts. If it isn't documented, it isn't done. A leader of distributed teams. You've hired and built trust with on-site engineers spread across many locations, most of whom you won't see day to day. You know how to create accountability, consistent standards and a shared culture across sites, both remotely and in person. Firm with partners. You hold colocation providers and vendors to high standards without becoming adversarial. You know the contract, you track performance, and you escalate when it's warranted. Compliance-minded without being a compliance specialist. You understand why access controls and decommissioning chain of custody are audit controls. You treat compliance as part of doing the work well, not as overhead. Automation-first. When something hurts, your first instinct is to fix the process or the tooling, not add people. You can turn an operational pain point into requirements engineering teams can act on. Required Experience 6+ years in data center operations, including 3+ years directly managing on-site technical teams. At least part of that time should be leading geographically distributed teams. A track record of operating multi-site data center fleets at hyperscale or large-cloud scale. Hands-on experience with IT hardware, including servers, network devices, optics and cabling, not only facilities infrastructure. Enough hands-on depth to coach engineers on technical work and to judge the quality of vendor and contractor work. Experience owning sites across the full lifecycle: delivering greenfield data center or cage builds through third-party vendors, running them in steady state, and decommissioning hardware. Experience managing providers in Tier III+ colocation facilities and holding them accountable to commitments. Experience managing 24x7 on-call operations and incident escalation. Strong Layer 1 and Layer 2 fundamentals: structured cabling, fiber and optics, patching standards, switching basics, and troubleshooting physical connectivity for network and server hardware. Solid knowledge of data center power and cooling, rack design, high-density deployments and hardware lifecycle management. Strong understanding of DCIM and asset management systems. You should have a track record of keeping documentation accurate from day one, including rack, power, cabling and asset records maintained from hardware arrival through decommissioning. Working knowledge of the security and compliance frameworks common in enterprise-grade data centers. You should understand them well enough to run operations under them; auditor-level expertise isn't required. Strong program management skills across multiple vendors, sites and time-bound workstreams. A track record of reducing toil through tooling or process redesign. Excellent written and verbal communication, including regular business reviews and status, risk and availability reporting to leadership. Ability to travel regularly to data center sites. Expect more frequent travel during site builds, shifting to periodic visits as sites reach steady state. Experience with PagerDuty or similar on-call and incident tooling. Experience with remote-hands programs and vendor scorecards. Background in hardware diagnostics, burn-in or automated build validation. Amazon:10582791.description:
Description As an ITS Support Engineer, you'll be the go-to knowledge expert for Amazon's corporate employees’, providing seamless end-to-end services and frictionless on-site technical support ensuring productivity remains secure and uninterrupted. Amazon’s ITS Support Engineers are dedicated, dependable and customer focused, owning the overall IT experience. They guarantee our employees have the tools and resources they need to be successful, innovative and efficient. ITS Support Engineers have an advanced understanding of IT standards, systems and equipment deployed throughout Amazon. They can work independently or collaborate with partner teams and contractors managing projects while maintaining a high level of productivity to meet goals. Quickly adapting to new processes and procedures, they act as a mentor and main partner for escalations within the team. Your day will be filled with exciting challenges and opportunities to showcase your technical expertise. You’ll engage with Amazonians across various teams, owning and recognizing their unique IT needs and provide personalized high-quality support. You'll be a trusted advisor, a problem-solver, taking initiative to diagnose, troubleshoot and resolve a wide variety of specialized hardware and software issues implementing successful solutions. Amazon:10582606.description:
Description As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center. Key job responsibilities Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems. Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center. Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved. Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders. Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers. Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders. Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers. Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholders’ management. Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers. Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team. Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces. Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations. Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts. Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation and/or under construction data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes. A day in the life As a Data Center Controls Engineer, your primary customers are Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO), who depend on you to deliver reliable, well integrated Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS). The problems you solve are technical: modifying controls logic to address operational issues, developing Methods of Procedure (MOPs) for firmware upgrades, or investigating complex alarm discrepancies across monitoring systems. For new builds, you own the controls scope from vendor submittal review through commissioning and turnover. You manage vendor relationships, budgets, and schedules for both service contracts and capital projects. Your internal stakeholders include your Controls Manager, Controls Technicians you provide technical direction to, and partner teams (Construction, Critical Projects Implementation, Commissioning, DCEO). About the team AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. Amazon:10582761.title: Sr. Security Engineer, Leo Security
Amazon:10582761.description:
Description We are open to hiring candidates to work out of one of the following locations: Redmond, WA, USA Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband network connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Have you wanted an opportunity to secure an advanced satellite based broadband telecom service? The Leo Security team owns the security of product and operations of Leo end-to-end. We provide the necessary infrastructure and mechanisms to ensure the security of our satellite constellation and to protect the integrity and confidentiality of our customer data. Our team drives the research & development, deployment and operation of several mission-critical security systems and mechanisms. You will work in a start-up like environment, backed by Amazon’s infrastructure to bootstrap security mechanisms, and help instill the security culture in the organization. Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities You and your team own the vulnerability management program for Leo systems across a large and heterogeneous fleet. The discovery, prioritization, and remediation actions themselves run on Amazon-wide mechanisms; your responsibility is to make sure those mechanisms actually work for Leo's unique fleet requirements, that coverage and risk-based prioritization hold up against how our systems are really built, and that gaps get closed. You will drive resolution of the high-severity and systemic vulnerabilities that matter most by coordinating across the teams that own them, and you will lead the burn down of long-term technical debt and risk so the fleet gets measurably safer over time. You will be a guardian for security simplicity. Leo's builders should inherit security at scale in ways that are easy to consume and that do not pile on untold burden or distract from shipping a game-changing satellite internet service, and it is your job to make sure that promise holds. You will collect feedback from the builders living with these mechanisms, detect where security is becoming friction instead of a default, and push to simplify it, so that doing the secure thing stays the path of least resistance rather than a tax on building. You will partner with builder teams and their leaders as a trusted advisor, helping them understand their risk, define security priorities, and secure their systems without slowing their delivery. You will assess technical debt and risk alongside them, provide strategic direction that addresses vulnerabilities and fortifies our products, help leaders measure their organization's security execution, and guide teams toward outcomes that produce products which safely handle customer data. Beyond any single engagement, you will instill a security culture that makes secure practices a default rather than an afterthought, and you will mentor builders who aspire to become security advocates and security engineers through 1-1 sessions and office hours, growing the next generation of security talent across the organization. You will translate compliance and regulatory requirements into concrete, auditable engineering controls and evidence, keeping Leo continuously audit-ready rather than scrambling before each review. You will define and report the metrics that show whether the program is working, including coverage, time-to-remediate, SLA adherence, and residual risk, and you will use that data to drive decisions. A day in the life In this highly dynamic role, you will join a team that is collectively accountable for where our security investments deliver the most value and most simplify security for Leo's builders. Together you will decide where to focus, challenge each other's priorities, and share the hard problems rather than carry them alone. No two days look the same, and the judgment the team brings to where it spends its attention is at the heart of the job. Teams will reach out for ideas on how to handle a wide variety of security problems, and you will be the person they trust to point them at the right answer. You can anticipate implementation questions like "What is the paved path for vulnerability management?", "This finding is flagged on my service but I think it is a false positive, how do I confirm it?", "I have a patch SLA I cannot meet without downtime, what are my options?", or "How do I keep this class of vulnerability from coming back?" You will help them cut through the noise, understand what actually matters for their systems, and get unblocked without slowing their delivery. When you are not responding to builder teams, you will step back and evaluate overall org performance to find the architectural defects behind recurring findings. Rather than chasing each ticket, you will look for the pattern underneath: a misconfiguration that keeps reappearing across the fleet, a dependency that drags a whole class of services below the bar, a gap in coverage where risk is going undetected. You will propose new security scanning capability and threat detections to close those gaps, and you will push to fix problems at the source so they stop generating work for everyone downstream. You will spend time in the data, reading the metrics that tell you whether the program is actually working: where remediation is stalling, which teams are trending the wrong way, where an SLA is about to slip, and where residual risk is concentrating. You will turn that signal into action, whether that means tuning how Amazon-wide mechanisms apply to Leo's fleet, driving a targeted campaign to burn down a specific risk, or raising a systemic issue to the leaders who own it. When a high-severity or systemic vulnerability lands, you will coordinate the response across every team that owns a piece of it and drive it to closure. Through all of it, you will help Amazon maintain a high bar for customer security. Every mechanism you tune, every gap you close, and every builder you unblock adds up to a fleet that is measurably safer and a security experience that stays simple enough that builders can keep shipping. About the team Diverse Experiences Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying. Why Amazon Security? At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores. Inclusive Team Culture In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices. Training & Career Growth We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Greenhouse: Cloudflare:8274068.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Location: Austin, TX San Francisco, CA About the Team Our sales team members work hand-in-hand with large organizations around the world to keep their digital environments protected. We educate, inspire, and empower our potential clients in their journey to security. As part of our sales team, you are empowered with systems and tools, constantly updated research and sales libraries, and a team built on joint success. You won't find someone at Cloudflare that isn't committed to your success - with everyone pitching in to assist when it comes to solutions selling, learning, and development. As a member of our sales team, you are motivated by a solutions-focused sales environment and find fulfillment in working with clients to resolve incredibly complex cyberthreats. This position has working hours Monday to Friday 09:00 a.m. to 06:00 p.m. Occasionally, we support our customers during the weekends for specific changes that need to be done outside of their business hours. Travel is expected at 30%. About the role: The Services Sales Manager (SSM) is a dynamic sales professional, passionate about technology evangelism and developing custom services solutions to drive business growth. This role owns sizing the service component of a Cloudflare opportunity. The SSM takes the technical solution and the customer requirements to deliver a Professional Services commercial proposition presenting customers with a clear line of sight from the solution to measurable business value, and giving sales teams the technical credibility to close. A core objective of the SSM is to grow the Cloudflare professional services business. This involves direct engagement with customers to define the specific service requirements needed to maximize the value of their technology investment and achieve their desired technical and business outcomes. The SSM works in a fast-paced environment and is instrumental in enabling Cloudflare customers to securely achieve their goals. This is accomplished by creating and proposing  a comprehensive services wrapper tailored to meet each customer's unique needs. The SSM maintains close working relationships across the organisation, partnering directly with the Account Teams, Specialist Sales, as well as establishing strong connections with Delivery teams, Global Delivery Practices, and other subject matter experts within Cloudflare Professional Services. The successful candidate will recommend the appropriate blend of Cloudflare services to assist customers in planning and executing large-scale transformations, ensuring they leverage maximum value from the portfolio. Showcase our delivery capabilities, IP, and expertise through compelling success stories that demonstrate how we solve customer needs. Gathering, understanding and defining customer specific requirements and expectations for value based outcomes in workshop based scenarios. Collaborating with Services Sales, Delivery and Global Practices to construct solution proposals and Statements of Work to satisfy customer specific scope requirements and outcome based services. Collaborating with Services Sales to drive business growth for Cloudflare Services in your aligned territory. Strong written, verbal and presentation skills. Demonstrated experience in discovery/scope definition workshops with cross–functional internal and customer resources to prepare current state/future state roadmaps and services proposals. Experience of working across multiple regions. Cybersecurity experience preferred. Experience and familiarity with using SFDC or similar CRM tools. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Amazon:10583242.description:
Description Do you want to solve solve business challenges through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services where your code has a direct, measurable impact? The Zamboni team sits at the intersection of software and physical hardware, managing the fleet of custom Glacier storage units that power Amazon S3's cold storage at exabyte scale. As an SDE I on this team, you'll build and operate the NAWS-based automation that keeps 2,000+ Glacier storage units healthy across global regions — from firmware deployment pipelines to break-fix remediation workflows to the operator tooling that other teams rely on every day. This is hands-on systems work with real stakes. When a Glacier storage unit goes offline in IAD, your code is part of the response. When a firmware rollout needs to scale across a global fleet, your automation makes it safe. You'll work closely to solve problems that span the full stack — from DynamoDB concurrency to custom storage hardware. At Amazon, we hire engineers who think big and want to define what comes next. Every day brings new challenges, new skills, and the kind of growth that's hard to find elsewhere. If you want your software to directly impact infrastructure that millions of customers depend on, this is the role. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, and operate NAWS-based services (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, SQS) that automate Glacier fleet operations including firmware deployment, library onboarding, hardware monitoring, and break-fix remediation - Contribute to automation projects that reduce manual operational toil — including automated offline library remediation, drive blocklisting, stuck job workflows, and automated ticket escalation - Build and maintain operator tooling and Fleet Commander integrations that enable safe, auditable fleet operations at scale - Collaborate with hardware vendors (BDT, Quantum), DCO technicians, partner with other S3 Keystone and Glacier teams to design solutions that bridge software and physical hardware - Participate in on-call rotations, respond to operational events, and drive improvements that reduce future toil - Write high-quality Java/Python/Go code with infrastructure defined in CDK A day in the life On any given day you might be debugging why a firmware update stalled on a Glacier storage library in IAD, writing a new step function workflow to automate a remediation path, reviewing a design doc for the next phase of Fleet automation, or working through a tricky DynamoDB concurrency issue. The work spans from low-level hardware interactions to distributed NAWS service design. You'll be on-call, you'll ship real automation, and you'll see the direct impact of your work on Glacier storage fleet availability. About the team The Zamboni team, part of the S3 Moirai organization, owns the health and availability of Glacier's custom storage hardware: libraries, firmware, fleet automation, and the operator tooling that keeps Glacier running at 99.95% data availability across 12+ regions worldwide. AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. The AWS GCNA (Global Connectivity and Network Availability) Organization is looking for a Network Development Engineer to join our EDGE team. Network Development Engineers partner with our broader Infrastructure organization on configurations standards and tools, and collaborate with Systems and Software Engineers to ensure fast, smooth roll-out of new designs and products, and also deploy and sustain networking software tools. AWS GCNA (Global Connectivity and Network Availability) is the backbone that connects the global AWS network. Focused on controlling the internet traffic that allows users to access their information and applications regardless of where they are in the world. GCNA is responsible for building and designing a complex backbone network that allows internet traffic to flow efficiently between data centers and customers. Key job responsibilities Network Development Engineers will: •	Be responsible for deploying network infrastructure across all of our network fabrics that supports the Amazon Retail Service, Kindle, Payments and multiple AWS services. •	Deploy, scale and automate our network across multiple global datacenters. This includes existing footprints and greenfield locations. •	Drive scaling of current network designs to meet the demand of our customers. •	Create simple, repetitive deployment processes that increase both velocity and quality. •	Work closely with our internal customers on designs/solutions; bringing those designs/solutions from concept to production. •	Create and update our network standards and ensure that the network is deployed to these standards. •	Create and implement changes on the network. •	Work closely with our automation teams in defining the tools that allow us to scale at higher volume. A day in the life Engineers in the Internet Edge organization have a wide range of responsibilities: we evolve routing policy, implement traffic engineering solutions, grow our peering footprint, secure the “front door” from bad actors on the Internet, and architect the hardware platforms and network design to support any Amazon product that needs to reach end-users worldwide. Our infrastructure moves terabits of traffic to and from the Internet at any given moment, and represents one of the largest edge surface areas in the world, requiring complex solutions to ensure that capacity always stays ahead of demand. To accomplish that, our engineers develop automation, write software, and work with a wide range of partner teams to continually improve and automate our Internet connectivity in areas such as capacity delivery, configuration deployment, impairment detection, and traffic optimization. Internet Edge engineers make decisions on both a day-to-day and long-term strategic basis, which carry a large amount of responsibility and impact across all of Amazon’s products. •	Support an off-hours operations escalation pager rotation. •	Manage customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure. •	Sit at the computer during scheduled work hours with appropriate breaks while maintaining a high level of alertness and attention to detail. •	Travel to data center/network sites and Amazon/customer offices as needed. Within AWS Networking, the Internet Edge organization is responsible for connecting Amazon to the global Internet. With connections to thousands of unique external networks in hundreds of locations across the world, our mission is to deliver an Internet connectivity experience that sets the global standard for performance, availability, security, and cost, making Amazon the clear choice for our customers’ needs.

Amazon:10584479.title: Software Development Engineer II
Amazon:10584479.description:
Description Most cloud engineers never see the physical world their software touches. On this team, you will. We build the networking that carries AWS out of the cloud and into customers' own data centers—so a hospital, a factory, or a bank can run AWS right next to the systems and data that can't leave the building. When you ship here, your code is soon routing real production traffic on real hardware in the field, all over the world. In this role you'll design and build the services that keep that traffic flowing, and you'll own them all the way through—not just writing the code, but operating it, watching how it behaves in production, and making it more reliable over time. You'll dig into genuinely hard problems in distributed systems and networking, where the failure modes are interesting and the impact of a fix is immediate and visible. You'll also help us work smarter, not just harder: a real part of the job is building AI agents and automation that take the repetitive engineering and operational work off the team's plate, so everyone can spend more time on the problems that actually need human judgment. If you like owning things end to end, want your work to matter in the physical world, and enjoy making a team faster as you go, you'll fit right in. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, test, and operate scalable, highly available control plane, distribution, and data plane services that route production traffic for AWS Outposts deployments worldwide. - Own significant components end to end—from design documents and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and long-term operational health. - Take ambiguous, loosely defined problems and drive them to well-reasoned technical designs, making sound tradeoffs with limited guidance. - Write, update, and improve AI agents and automation that increase software-development and operational efficiency—reducing manual toil so the team can focus on high-judgment work. - Raise the operational bar: improve observability, harden deployment pipelines, and drive down the time-to-detect and time-to-mitigate for the systems you own. - Participate in an on-call rotation for the services you own, and lead the investigation and resolution of production issues, including root-cause analysis and long-term corrective actions. - Write high-quality, well-tested, maintainable code and hold a high bar in design and code reviews. - Brainstorm ideas with teammates and review key technical decisions and designs with senior engineers and leadership to pressure-test approaches and align on direction. - Mentor junior engineers, share context generously, and contribute to the technical direction and engineering standards of the team. - Collaborate across teams—partner service teams (e.g., S3, EBS, Route 53), networking, and hardware/edge teams—to deliver features that span organizational boundaries. A day in the life Most of your day is spent designing, building, and operating the services that route traffic for AWS Outposts and Local Gateway, keeping them running reliably for customers around the world. You'll write and review code, and you'll keep an eye on your dashboards to make sure the changes you ship are flowing safely into production and everything you own is healthy. You'll also spend real time making the team faster: building and improving AI agents and automation that take routine engineering and operational work off everyone's plate, so we can focus on the harder, more interesting problems. Ideas come from everywhere here, so expect to brainstorm with teammates, sketch out approaches together, and talk through your bigger technical decisions with experienced engineers and leaders who'll help you sharpen your thinking. You'll also work closely with partner teams like S3, EBS, and Route 53 to ship things that span more than one service. Beyond the day-to-day, you'll have the room to dig into ambiguous problems, decide how the services you own should evolve, and help the engineers around you grow. Because our software runs in customer data centers all over the world, you'll see the real impact of your work quickly—and you'll have a genuine say in how we make it more reliable and easier to operate over time. About the team Our team is focused on building reliable, scalable software that customers depend on every day. We value collaboration, clear communication, and a commitment to getting the details right. We believe that great software comes from inclusive teams where every voice is heard and good ideas can come from anyone. As we look ahead, we are investing in new capabilities and technologies that will expand our impact, and you will play a key role in shaping that direction. If you are excited about solving hard problems alongside thoughtful engineers, we would love to hear from you.

Greenhouse: Cloudflare:8304060.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Austin, TX or Raleigh, NC About the Department Account Executives, Channel Account Managers, Business Development Representatives, Solution Engineers, Customer Success, and Sales Operations - all working together help our customers adopt Cloudflare and create great Internet-enabled experiences. The sales team at Cloudflare helps customers solve real, technical problems while creating the revenue streams that help the company provide free service to millions in our community. About this Role AEs are positioned to drive in-depth product discussions while communicating and demonstrating value quickly to customers.  This role within this segment focuses on both the acquisition of prospective Commercial accounts, as well as the expansion of existing customer accounts.  The ideal candidate will have both a sales and technical background that enables them to drive customer engagement from technical professionals through to senior executive levels, and across Security, Network, Development and Infrastructure teams. Key Responsibilities Develop, execute, and maintain your territory plan to exceed quarterly sales targets and annual quota assignment. Be an expert in three unique sales motions; new business acquisition (new customer logos), customer expansion (upsell and cross sell Cloudflare solutions), and renewal within your territory. Build a robust sales pipeline utilizing the four sourcing funnels: AE led outbound, BDR, Channel, and Marketing Inbound. Develop and strategically leverage a deep technical understanding of the problems Cloudflare solves in order to drive a consultative sales motion. Craft and communicate compelling value propositions for Cloudflare services. Drive awareness through regular outbound campaigns on product and feature roadmap updates. Accurately forecast, build commercial outcomes by running a consistent sales process, including driving next step expectations and contract negotiations. As a trusted advisor, build long-term strategic relationships with key accounts, to ensure customer adoption, retention and expansion. Regularly evaluate usage trends and articulate value to show Cloudflare impact and provide strategic recommendations during business reviews. Network across different business units with each of your accounts, and multi-thread to identify and engage new divisional buyers. Position Cloudflare's platform in each of your target customers, including Cloudflare One and the Connectivity Cloud to realize our full potential in every customer. Operate internally as a liaison with cross-functional teams to share key customer feedback and insights to improve customer experience and further investments with Cloudflare. Requirements: 3+ years sales experience selling B2B SaaS Strong B2B discovery skills Candidates have a point of view of industry trends and able to customize a client centric why change narrative Track record of beating annual targets of $1M+ and successfully managing complex six figure deals Experienced in multithreading into the C-suite and across an organization to manage a complex sales cycle Self-motivated; entrepreneurial spirit Bachelor's degree required Software and system skills are a must (SFDC, Tableau, G-suite, MSFT suite) Ability to travel up to 25% of the time. What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! Imagine developing the foundational technology behind tomorrow’s AI factories, next-generation data centers, autonomous platforms—and even data centers in space. You will join a world-class team building and maintaining software for complex heterogeneous computing systems that power groundbreaking AI, HPC, and accelerated computing workloads. Your work will help bring sophisticated server products from early silicon through deployment while improving their performance, reliability, power efficiency, and serviceability.

This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of hardware, firmware, operating systems, and AI. You will collaborate with some of the best engineers in the world to solve challenging system-level problems and redefine what future data center products can achieve. If you are a creative software engineer who is passionate about low-level technology and wants to build products that expand the boundaries of computing, we want to hear from you. Join us at the forefront of this new frontier!

  


What you’ll be doing:

  * Design and develop SoC software, validation solutions, and test frameworks that efficiently validate and stress complex SoCs and systems throughout the complete software development lifecycle. Your work may span user space, the kernel, firmware, and SoC boot software.
  * Pioneer next-generation system validation and reliability software that accelerates the journey from virtual prototypes and first silicon to production-ready hardware, large-scale deployment, and rapid failure resolution across standard and custom platforms.
  * Spearhead initiatives that improve the efficiency, intelligence, robustness, and user experience of software used for design validation, thermal and power characterization, manufacturing screening, and customer platform bring-up.
  * Investigate and drive root-cause analysis of highly complex board- and system-level failures across hardware and software boundaries.

What we need to see:

  * BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  * 8+ years of relevant industry experience.
  * Strong C and C++ programming skills, including object-oriented design and development.
  * Experience with low-level systems software, device drivers, firmware, or hardware-facing programming.
  * A strong understanding of processor architecture fundamentals, preferably ARM.
  * Exceptional problem-solving and debugging skills, particularly for issues spanning multiple layers of the system.
  * Excellent communication, interpersonal, and planning skills, with the ability to lead technically complex initiatives.

  


Ways to stand out from the crowd:

NVIDIA:893398235104.title: Senior Systems Software Engineer, Workload Systems Engineering
NVIDIA:893398235104.description:
NVIDIA is seeking a senior systems software engineer to help engineering teams run demanding build, simulation, and validation workloads efficiently and reliably. Our Workload Systems Engineering team connects customer workflows with the infrastructure that performs them. We develop self-service mechanisms and clear diagnostics, investigate performance and reliability across system boundaries, and deliver measured infrastructure improvements with the teams that own the underlying components.

  


Your responsibilities include enabling application configuration, remote execution, workers, hosts, GPU and CPU resources, storage, data paths, and on-target systems. The position requires direct system evaluation: diagnosing causes of slow or failing workloads, trying alternatives in representative scenarios, applying improvements with others, and verifying customer advantages.

  


What you'll be doing:

  * Build shared self-service and validation mechanisms that let engineering teams configure and use supported infrastructure workflows with less manual assistance.
  * Give customers and on-call teams useful diagnostic views across application, submission, remote-execution, and host or target layers so they can identify where failures and slowdowns originate.
  * Set performance and reliability benchmarks for representative workloads. Apply profiling, metrics, traces, and controlled experiments to pinpoint the changes that make a difference.
  * Evaluate and improve compute and GPU selection, scheduling and placement, concurrency, worker and runner configuration, resource sharing, caching, and input/output paths.
  * Make retry causes, recovery outcomes, and wasted execution capacity visible. Work with component owners to eliminate recurring failures and unnecessary re-execution.
  * Implement and validate infrastructure-level changes with application, build and CI, remote-execution, and infrastructure teams. Measure the effect on turnaround, successful efficiency, stability, usable capacity, and cost.
  * Turn successful investigations into supported workflows, diagnostics, documentation, and clear customer handoffs.

  


What we need to see:

  * Over 8 years of solid software engineering experience working with production compute infrastructure, distributed systems, large-scale build and test systems, or comparable systems software.
  * Hands-on experience debugging complex performance or reliability issues across software and hardware boundaries using logs, metrics, traces, profiling, and experiments.
  * Proficiency in a systems programming or automation language and experience delivering tested changes into production infrastructure.
  * In-depth experience with Linux and proficiency in one or more of these fields: GPU systems and drivers, scheduling and resource management, remote execution or CI infrastructure, storage and data paths, or host and container infrastructure.
  * Ability to work across teams with different component ownership, turn ambiguous symptoms into a clear technical plan, and explain results to engineering customers.
  * A degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  


Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  * Experience with GPU sharing and isolation, CUDA execution behavior, MIG or MPS or equivalent experience, GPU driver diagnostics, or high-performance computing workloads.
  * Experience with workload placement, CPU and GPU concurrency, NUMA, cloud-instance benchmarking, or cost and performance tradeoffs.
  * Familiarity with Bazel, remote execution, build front ends, simulation or replay workloads, and hardware-in-the-loop validation.
  * Experience improving file-system, caching, networking, or high-throughput data paths under concurrent workloads.

NVIDIA:893398245783.description:
Securing NVIDIA's EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying a standard security stack. The workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for an off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. You'll be an individual contributor on Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters, the team that implements security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA's hardware engineers design silicon on - spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud. You will sit alongside the engineers who run these clusters 24x7, close enough to deploy a control, investigate a behavior, and change the running environment yourself.

  


This is hands-on build work, not control review. You'll decide where conventional tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and then engineer the alternative. If your depth is in large-scale compute, networking, or storage infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job, and you've carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you're who we want to talk to. We don't expect fluency in every security product category. We expect you to own outcomes and pick up the remaining domain breadth fast. Security engineering here is engineering: code, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure - not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.

  


What You'll Be Doing:

  * Build and operate security controls and telemetry for EDA compute, storage, and networking - design, ship to production, then own them.
  * Engineer around hard constraints. Protect multi-day, high-value compute jobs without degrading them. Where heavyweight in-node agents are not viable, build the workable answer instead.
  * Make the network and platform the control plane. Protection can't depend solely on what runs inside the node.
  * Instrument for detection. Collect and normalize security signals from the fleet into our SIEM, and build the detections and dashboards that turn it into something actionable. Log collection alone is not monitoring.
  * Investigate and respond. Chase down EDA-specific threats and exposure, and execute containment and remediation hands-on with infrastructure and service owners.
  * Automate enforcement and evidence. Infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state, with compliance evidence produced as an engineering output rather than a manual exercise.
  * Run the lifecycle of the security technologies you own: selection, rollout, operation, and eventual replacement.
  * Work across boundaries. Partner directly with data center operations, IT storage and networking, network engineering, CSP teams, and NVIDIA's central security organization on shared outcomes.
  * Think like an adversary. Threat modeling and mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.

  


What We Need To See:

  * 8+ years of hands-on infrastructure or infrastructure-security engineering across on-prem and cloud environments.
  * Strong Linux depth - you are comfortable at the system level, not just the console level.
  * Real experience operating or securing compute fleets at scale: provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running jobs.

Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:

We are seeking a Security Research Engineer to advance our Validate and Patch capabilities by establishing what counts as a confirmed vulnerability and defining what constitutes a truly correct, safe fix. In this critical role, you will apply rigorous security judgment to well-defined categories of vulnerabilities. These affect NVIDIA-internal targets. Ultimately, we hold our results to an exceptionally high bar and value specific, verifiable proof of your technical expertise—such as CVEs, advisories, or original security tools—over polished phrasing.

  * Validation methods: Develop techniques that confirm vulnerabilities are real and reachable.

  * Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) with 12+ years in security research or software engineering.

Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

  


NVIDIA is seeking a Senior Systems Software Engineer for the Apache Spark Acceleration group. GPU accelerated data processing has moved from proof of concept to production deployments. Enterprises now recognize the need for accelerated computing to handle large data processing needs. Multi-node GPU deployments reduce cloud computing costs and lower the latency of batch ETL workloads. At NVIDIA, we accelerate Apache Spark with an open source plugin that speeds up Spark applications on GPUs without code changes, and our cuDF Spark library is integrated with AWS EMR, Databricks, Google Dataproc, Oracle Cloud Data Flow, Bytedance Volcengine, Tencent Cloud and Cloudera. This role is on the team that runs that acceleration as a handled Spark service inside NVIDIA. The service accomplishes production data pipelines for NVIDIA’s internal data platform at thousands of jobs an hour on Kubernetes and AWS, under a customer SLA. It packages the cuDF Spark plugin and a CPU/GPU workload router into an API-based service built on Spark Connect, Kyuubi, Helm and Flux. You will work across all three layers: the service, the GPU Spark runtime, and the router.

  


What you’ll be doing:

  * Design, build and operate hosted Spark service control plane on Kubernetes: the Java REST API, the Spark Connect runner, Kyuubi, and deployment using Helm charts and Flux 
  * Own code review for one or more services end to end and keep them releasable on the release train
  * Extend the cuDF Spark runtime and the CPU/GPU workload router in Scala and Java, including interoperability with Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg and Unity Catalog
  * Investigate production failures on clusters running more than a thousand concurrent jobs together with the customer team and upstream library teams, and drive fixes to closure
  * Instrument metrics, dashboards and alerts; take part in the on-call rotation and keep the runbooks current
  * Provide recommendations and feedback to teams regarding decisions surrounding topics such as infrastructure, continuous integration and testing strategy

  


What we need to see:

  * BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field (or equivalent experience)
  * 9+ years of experience in software development
  * Strong distributed-systems fundamentals and proficiency in Java or Scala, plus C++ or Python
  * Hands-on experience operating services on Kubernetes, on-premise or cloud
  * Experience owning or reviewing a long-lived server: REST front ends, proxies or request routers, JDBC or Thrift services
  * Experience supporting enterprise or internal production customers, including on-call
  * Experience using AI tools in software development

  


Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  * Apache Spark internals, Spark Connect, or Kyuubi
  * Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg or Unity Catalog integration work
  * GPU data processing with cuDF, or CUDA experience
  * Significant contributions to data platform projects committed to collaboration and shared development (Apache Spark, Velox, Presto, Apache Arrow, Apache DataFusion)

NVIDIA:893398245843.description:
NVIDIA is seeking a motivated and creative Senior Verification Engineer to join our Tegra SoC IP Verification team. Our mission is to build the IP that enables the next generation of scalable, high-performance, multi-chip computing platforms. In this role, you will work closely with architecture and design teams to verify complex High Speed Coherent Interconnect Hub IP. You will help define verification strategies, develop robust verification environments, drive functional and performance verification, close coverage, and ensure high-quality design signoff. This position provides an opportunity to work on technologies at the heart of NVIDIA's next-generation computing platforms.

  


What You’ll Be Doing:

  * Develop and maintain verification infrastructure, including testbenches, BFMs, checkers, monitors, scoreboards, assertions, and constrained-random stimulus.
  * Define, review, and complete verification test plans for coherency protocol, ordering, error handling, performance, and other key IP features.
  * Verify protocol compliance and interoperability across complex SoC and multi-chip interfaces.
  * Develop and complete performance test plans to validate bandwidth, latency, QoS, and other performance requirements.
  * Drive functional and code coverage closure and provide to verification signoff.
  * Debug complex RTL and verification issues and work closely with architecture and design teams to drive them to resolution.
  * Collaborate with FPGA, emulation, software, and post-silicon teams to support system validation and silicon bring-up.

  


What We Need to See:

  * BS / MS or equivalent experience.
  * 3+ years of ASIC verification experience with complex IPs or SoC subsystems.
  * Strong background in SystemVerilog, UVM, constrained-random verification, and coverage-driven verification methodologies.
  * Experience developing verification environments, checkers, assertions, and functional coverage.
  * Strong debugging and problem-solving skills with experience using industry-standard simulation and debug tools.

  


Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  * Experience verifying high-speed coherent interconnects, NoCs, or other complex SoC infrastructure IP.
  * Knowledge of coherent interconnect protocols and technologies such as CHI and AXI.
  * Strong understanding of cache coherency, transaction ordering, and system-level data flows.
  * Experience with performance verification, including bandwidth, latency, QoS, and traffic management.
  * Strong scripting skills in Python, Perl, or Shell, along with excellent communication and collaboration skills.

NVIDIA:893398225799.title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, Open Models
NVIDIA:893398225799.description:
Do you want to help the world build custom AI? We're hiring a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer to drive technical engagement with partners and customers across NVIDIA's open model portfolio, including NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos. The mission is to turn open models into production-ready AI tuned to a specific domain, from post-training through harness optimization. We want any organization to build, own, and run its own AI on open source models, and this role helps the ecosystem get there at scale!

  


Unlike most forward deployed roles, our work runs primarily through NVIDIA's partner ecosystem. Our FDEs work side by side with top ecosystem engineering and research teams, co-lead joint customer engagements, and build the recipes and playbooks that help partners succeed and scale. We also work directly with customers when the work calls for it. Are you one of the strongest post-training applied researchers you know? Ready to take a model from a first customer conversation all the way to production? We'd love to meet you.

  
What you'll be doing:

  * This role drives AI solutions from discovery and scoping through post-training, harness optimization, and deployment, working alongside partners and customers. Each use case becomes a post-training and harness strategy with the right methods, data, evaluation, and success criteria. Scalable architectures and deployment plans then take the model to production.
  * The work is hands-on, as we build together with the ecosystem. Custom AI takes skill across the full stack, and we work across all of it: designing evaluations, building synthetic data pipelines, and post-training with LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning (synchronous and asynchronous). It also means making the architecture and hyperparameter choices that improve results. We tune the harness (prompting, tool use, orchestration, and context management) so the model shines in a specific domain, and we optimize inference so it runs cost-effectively in production.
  * You will lead technical engagements by scoping the work, shaping statements of work, and driving delivery with partner engineering teams and joint customers. We scale our impact by building reusable recipes, reference pipelines, and playbooks that let partners succeed independently and help the ecosystem mature in building domain-specific AI.
  * We connect NVIDIA's model research to partner and customer use cases, unlocking the post-trainability and inference cost-effectiveness of our models, and work with our product, research, and engineering teams to bring field insights back into Nemotron, Cosmos, and our software stack.
  * Above all, we're excited to help organizations worldwide build, own, and run their own AI on open source models!



  
What we need to see:

  * Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  * 8+ years in ML or software engineering, applied AI, FDE, or solutions architecture, including 3–5+ years of hands-on LLM post-training and taking models to production.
  * Solid fundamentals in deep learning and machine learning. Deep expertise in post-training methods, including LoRA/PEFT, SFT, and reinforcement learning, with an understanding of the trade-offs between RL synchronous and asynchronous approaches. Strong grasp of model architectures and hyperparameters and how they shape training outcomes.
  * Good understanding of large-scale distributed training and inference performance optimization. Ability to configure and tune workloads for memory efficiency, throughput, latency, and scaling across multi-GPU and multi-node systems.
  * Hands-on experience with post-training data, including synthetic data pipelines, dataset curation and filtering, and evaluation sets. Experience with harness engineering for LLM and agentic systems. Proficiency in PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Python, and Linux.
  * Proven ability to scope an engagement, shape an SOW, and lead delivery with partners and customers. Excellent organizational skills, empathy for partner and customer needs, and the ability to drive complex decisions across teams and companies through trusted relationships.
  * Clear communication of complex technical ideas, from engineers to C-level executives. Strong problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to partner and customer success.



  
Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  * A hands-on technical expert and problem solver who can clearly describe solution paths for complex challenges.
  * History of enabling partners and customers to successfully adopt open models and NVIDIA technologies and platforms.
  * A technical vision that influences product and engineering decisions and drives production outcomes.
  * Hands-on experience with Nemotron, Cosmos, and other open models, as well as both serverless and self-managed post-training platforms (e.g. Tinker APIs), including open-source frameworks such as NVIDIA NeMo and Megatron.
  * Experience with multimodal or world-foundation-model post-training, and running training jobs on large GPU clusters with SLURM or Kubernetes.

Available Locations: USA About the Team Cloudflare is changing how it grows and how it measures growth and Revenue and Consumption is becoming a core Go-To-Market (GTM) metric that shapes our GTM motions. The Consumption Transformation Team is the design engine for that change. Working closely with GTM leaders and the Developer leadership team, we help define the metric, draft and enforce the Rules of Engagement (ROE) for Consumption, build the analytics and field reporting, and support enablement, landing, and continuous improvement. We are a partnering team and aim to work cross functionally to support our internal functions successfully in a consumption business. This is a new team, so you will be building the way we work, and we expect successful candidates to use AI every day to take on more than a team this size normally could. About the Role You will turn the Consumption strategy into working models, trusted data, and clear answers for the field. You will design, build, and land the targeting models, build scorecards with our cross-functional partners and Data and Analytics Leader, give Geo Ops analytics they need to run their business, and be the first stop when our field teams seek clarity on our data, reporting, and use this to improve our models. What you'll do Design, model, and land targets: Build and evolve our target setting model, and own the methodology. Back-test them, land them with GTM leaders, and keep improving them. Execute the strategy: Take direction from the Strategy Lead and turn it into working methods and recommendations, and flag early when the data says the plan should change. Build scorecards: Work with our DIA and GTM Analytics teams to build and maintain scorecards with cross-functional partners covering field performance, data quality, and disputes. Protect data integrity: Validate actuals, baselines, targets, revenue attribution, and account ownership against source systems such as BigQuery, and tie GTM Revenue back to Finance and Billing. Support the field and apply the Rules of Engagement: Answer field questions and cases on baselines, quotas, crediting, and ownership, applying the Rules of Engagement consistently and keeping a record of each decision. Spot where a rule needs to change, and provide the account hierarchy and ownership data teams need to collaborate across geos on our most critical customers. Support territory planning and partner across teams: Provide analytics to Geo Ops and central territory design so they can deliver successful territory and coverage plans with equitable distribution of opportunity and targets. Work with Finance, Billing, data engineering, IT, RevOps, and Compensation to define data needs and move manual spreadsheet work into governed data products. Use AI to scale the work: Use AI tools, to write and review SQL, speed up reconciliations, draft answers to common field questions, and automate recurring checks. Review every result for accuracy and follow Cloudflare policy on confidential data. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. NVIDIA:893396945834.description:
NVIDIA is dedicated to reinventing accelerated computing. Reinvention requires great technology and amazing people. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world. We are searching for a Senior Compiler Engineer in our GPU Software organization. We deliver features and improvements that help NVIDIA hardware reach its full potential across a growing range of computational workloads, from deep learning and scientific computing to self-driving cars, video games, and virtual reality. Our compiler organization makes its mark on every GPU NVIDIA produces.

  


The CUDA programming language defines a unified programming model across a range of system configurations and hardware capabilities. The compiler translates parallel programs written in higher-level languages, like CUDA C++, into microcode optimized for fast execution on NVIDIA’s family of industry-leading GPU architectures. More and more of that code is now written with the help of AI agents, and the compiler front end is where developers and agents first meet the language. In this role, you will focus on the CUDA compiler front end, building language features, diagnostics, and capabilities that help both developers and agents write correct, high-performance GPU code. You’ll also have the opportunity to grow into other parts of the compiler stack, including the LLVM-based optimizer, code generation, and MLIR.

  


What you'll be doing:

  * Build compiler capabilities that help AI agents generate high-performing, high-quality GPU code.
  * Improve front-end diagnostics and compiler feedback so that developers and AI agents can understand and act on what the compiler tells them.
  * Design and implement CUDA C++ language features and extensions in the compiler front end, including parsing, semantic analysis, and code generation to IR.
  * Track and implement evolving C++ standards features, and make sure they work well with the CUDA programming model.
  * Explore and contribute to all parts of the compiler stack, including optimization, back end, and MLIR, wherever the right solution lives.
  * Partner and collaborate with other compiler, library, and developer tools teams in a dynamic environment to deliver high-quality, robust solutions.

  


What we need to see:

  * Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience.
  * 5+ years of relevant work or research experience in compiler development.
  * Hands-on experience with a production C or C++ compiler front end, such as Clang or GCC.
  * Strong understanding of the C++ language, including templates, overload resolution, and modern C++ standards.
  * Strong C/C++ programming and software design skills.
  * Ability to work independently, define project goals and scope, and drive complex engineering efforts to production.
  * Solid interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate across teams.

  


Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  * Clang development experience, including upstream contributions.
  * Experience participating in programming language standards committees.
  * Experience with LLVM optimization passes, code generation, or MLIR dialects.
  * CUDA C++ application development experience and a deep understanding of parallel programming concepts.
  * Experience with compiler diagnostics, static analysis, or language tooling such as clangd.

  


With highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package, NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology industry's most desirable employers. We have some of the most brilliant and hardworking people in the world working with us and our product lines are growing fast in some of the hottest state of the art fields such as Virtual Reality, Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Autonomous Vehicles.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 152,000 USD - 241,500 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 24, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.
